tasks.short: Distribute menus, collect diet sheets, and deliver trays and snacks to patients.

steps.what: Collect diet sheets for the hospital patients
Match those diet sheets to the menus patients may eat

loop.input: The diet code, the allergen flags and any handwritten diet line.
loop.output: A tray list of dishes this patient may eat.
loop.check: Every dish is on today's menu, matches the diet code, and the handwritten allergy line excludes any dish that contains that allergen.
loop.stop: The food preparation worker accepts this list or rewrites it after two drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A code table cannot read a handwritten allergy line.

steps.what: File the accepted tray list before portioning
Portion food trays and snacks from the accepted list
Deliver food trays and snacks to nursing units
Distribute menus directly to the hospital patients

tasks.design: The paper sort shortens only because the ward clerk already keyed the diet code and allergen flags on the {OTHER} meal list, which fills a tray list in {DOCS}. The food preparation worker still reads the handwritten allergy line and accepts that list, and only the accepted version is filed. Portioning the trays, walking them to the ward, and handing the menu to the patient stay in person at full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diet notes are handwriting, and the wrong tray can harm a patient, so the match stayed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: A filter can hide dishes a stored diet code forbids, and a bounded read can draft the handwritten allergy line, with the worker accepting the list.
tasks.still_hard: The ward round, portioning, and any sheet that is still only paper.
tasks.human_edge: The worker still accepts the allergen reading and still carries the tray.

ambition.what: Which dishes a coded diet allows, on every tray, including diets that used to be matched from memory.

tasks.altitude: The ward round still happens. The worker still accepts every tray list before it is filed.

reach.task: Key the diet code and allergen flags before the kitchen portions
reach.learn: Which diet codes and allergen flags the meal list already stores.

evidence.claim: Menutech detects the 14 EU allergens on a menu, and a healthcare module hides dishes a resident may not eat. The worker still portions and delivers the tray.
Allergen information is mandatory for non-prepacked food, and the operator stays responsible for accuracy, so the tray list is not accepted on a model's word alone.
A patient's diet can reveal health or religion, which is special-category data, so the list uses the diet code the ward already stored.

In 2023 the inspectorate found 51.8 percent of horeca fell short and 30.7 percent of inspections found no allergen information. That source is horeca, not hospitals, which is why a person still accepts the list.
Matching a coded diet to today's menu is a filter on stored flags. The handwritten allergy line is the part a person still reads. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal hour is collecting and sorting diet sheets, matching them to the menu, filing the accepted list, portioning, delivering, and handing menus out. Patient time and ward-nurse time are not in this baseline.
Portioning, the walk to the nursing units, and handing menus to patients are in-person steps the design does not change, so each stays at remaining 100.

The meal-list fields the zeroed sort relies on are ward, bed or patient code, diet code, allergen flags, texture, nil-by-mouth, and a handwritten note. The producer is the ward clerk, who already keys the diet code and allergen flags for the ward before the kitchen portions. That keying is the clerk's existing time, not this worker's hour, and it is not a new hour.
If the sheet is still only paper, the worker types the diet code. That capture stays in this worker's time, and the list saving does not apply.
The match step shortens by half only because a filter hides dishes the stored diet code and allergen flags forbid. The remaining half is reading the handwritten allergy line and accepting the list.
Filing shortens only because it stores the version the worker already accepted. It is not a new judgement.
Allergen-map fields are a dish id and allergen flags from the ingredient specification. A person confirms each new specification. A model is never the last source of an allergen claim.
Menu cards are already printed by the diet kitchen. This task only hands them to the patient.
Test the native meal-list view before a custom screen.
The 2 incremental hours are diet-code and allergen-map upkeep when the menu changes, beyond the per-patient review.
unknowns: Whether wards already key diet codes before the kitchen portions.
Whether patients choose the menu or the diet kitchen assigns it.
research_questions: What share of wards still send a handwritten diet sheet?

already_counted.description: Portioning trays and snacks, walking them to the nursing units, and handing menus to patients stay in the remaining time.
Reading the handwritten allergy line and accepting the tray list stays in the match step.

incremental.description: Keep the diet-code and allergen map current when the menu changes, beyond the per-patient review in the tray-list step.

approvals.approved_version: tray list version the food preparation worker accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Portioning (32), the walk to nursing units (32) and handing menus to patients (8) stay at full time because the design does not change those steps. The paper sort (10) drops only when the ward clerk has already keyed the diet code and allergen flags. Half of the match (6 of 12) remains to read the handwritten allergy line. Filing (6) stores the version the worker already accepted. Gross 22 minus 2 hours of map upkeep is a net of 20. The high end, 9, is a ward where most diets are already coded. The low end, 2, is a ward that still sends paper sheets, so the worker types them and that capture is not removed. Delivery is not claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep records of the quantities of food used.

steps.what: Count the quantities of food used since the last entry
Enter those quantities into the food-use records
Decide which quantity gaps belong in the records
Post the accepted quantities on the food-use record

tasks.design: The store count stays a walk, and deciding which gap is real use stays a judgement at full time. The entry line shortens only when the institution cook has stored a recipe quantity and a tray or batch count already has portions produced: the {DOCS} line is filled as portions times that quantity, and the worker reviews it. The post writes only the accepted quantity. No camera records who discarded an item.
tasks.previous_blocker: Usage was a tally after the shift, and the recipe quantity and the portion count lived on different sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Portions times a stored recipe quantity is plain arithmetic. The person still judges the gap.
tasks.still_hard: A day with no portion count, and waste a recipe line cannot see.
tasks.human_edge: The worker decides which gap is real use.

ambition.what: Which gap between the counted use and the recipe quantity is posted.

tasks.altitude: The count still happens. The worker still accepts every quantity that is posted.

reach.task: Store the recipe quantity and read the posted food-use quantities before the next prep
reach.learn: Which ingredients the count showed as used above the recipe quantity.

evidence.claim: Orbisk weighs, photographs and identifies each discard. That covers waste, not every ingredient used in prep. This design does not use that camera.
Winnow identifies discards and also forecasts production per service. The forecast is not this food-use record, and this design does not use the camera.
Vermaat reported 44 percent less food waste, 11,693 kg avoided. The source gives no baseline period and does not measure time spent writing food-use records.
No Annex III point covers food records, so this quantity post is not a high-risk system on that annex.
A waste camera or an app that logs who did what observes staff and needs works-council consent. This design posts quantities and does not record who discarded an item.

assumptions: The focal hour is the store count, the entry of quantities, the gap decision, and the post. Cook time and clerk time are not in this baseline.
The store count and the gap decision are an in-person step and a judgement the design does not change, so each stays at remaining 100.
The entry line shortens by half only because it is filled as portions times a stored recipe quantity, and the worker still reviews the line. A code does not judge whether the gap is real.

The recipe quantity field is produced by the institution cook, who already stores it per portion for prep. That is the cook's existing time, not a new hour and not this worker's hour. If the recipe quantity is missing, the worker writes the counted use and the arithmetic fill does not apply.

Portions produced come from the tray count on the accepted tray list, or from the batch count the institution cook already wrote for the service. That count is existing work. If neither figure exists, the worker writes the quantity by hand and the fill does not apply.

The zeroed post relies on the accepted quantities this task's gap decision already produced. It stores the quantity and a version id. It does not store a photo tied to a person, and it does not record who discarded an item.
Test the native food-use log before a custom screen.
The 2 incremental hours are yield updates when a batch size changes, and corrections on lines the count still disputes.
unknowns: Whether portions produced are already counted before this record is written.
Whether today's log is a paper sheet or a document on screen.
research_questions: What share of food-use lines is a recipe times portions, versus a store count with no portion figure?

already_counted.description: The store count of quantities used stays a full walk.
Reviewing the filled quantity line stays on the entry step.
Deciding which quantity gap is real use stays in full.

incremental.description: Update recipe yields when a batch size changes, and correct lines the count still disputes.

approvals.approved_version: food-use quantity version the food preparation worker accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The store count (50) and the gap decision (18) stay at full time because the design does not change the walk or that judgement. The entry line drops by half (10 of 20) only when the institution cook has stored a recipe quantity and a tray or batch count already has portions produced; the worker still reviews the line. Posting (12) writes the accepted quantity. Gross 22 minus 2 hours of yield updates is a net of 20. The high end, 10, is a day when most lines match the recipe and only gaps are judged. The low end, 3, is a day with no portion count, so the worker still writes the quantities and the arithmetic fill does not apply. No camera time is claimed, and a waste-weight case is not a time saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still counting, portioning and walking trays to the ward. Less time goes to sorting paper diet sheets and retyping quantities. The food preparation worker still accepts every tray list and every quantity that is posted. A model does not have the last word on an allergen or a diet.
reach: Ward clerk: key the diet code and allergen flags before the kitchen portions, instead of sending a loose sheet.
Institution cook: store the recipe quantity and read the posted food-use quantities before the next prep list.
skills_to_grow: Check a tray list against the handwritten allergy line before accepting it.
Compare a recipe quantity with the counted use and record only the gap they can explain.
role.ambitious_version: Every tray leaves with a list the worker has accepted against the diet code, and the food-use record fills from portions times the recipe so the count is only for the gap.
